# Page/paragraph anchors inside table cells

Original XML controls generated by `tools/page_paragraph_cell_anchor_fixture.py`
from the repository's original table-global-anchor fixture. Twelve pages in each
of compatibility modes 15 and 12 cross page/margin horizontal coordinates,
layoutInCell true/false, and top/center/bottom cell alignment. Each picture is in
the second row and second paragraph of a padded cell. A leading row distinguishes
row and table origins. Explicit Arial runs and exact 24pt paragraph advances
isolate positioning from font fallback. No corpus artwork is included.

The reference application supplies the native PDFs and PNGs; all 24 image-bearing
page regions were inspected. `tools/record_page_paragraph_cell_anchors.py`
records source/PDF hashes and PDF image bounds in top-left point coordinates.
The 72 x 36pt image has offsets (10,12) pt. The reference application establishes:

- Mode 15, either layoutInCell value: page X=226pt, margin X=235pt. Only margin X
  includes the 9pt left cell margin. Y follows the second paragraph and vertical
  cell alignment, giving 158/194/230pt for top/center/bottom.
- Mode 12, layoutInCell=true: identical frames.
- Mode 12, layoutInCell=false: page X=10pt or margin X=82pt. Y=122pt, measured
  from the physical anchor row at 110pt, excluding 12pt top padding, preceding
  paragraphs and vertical alignment. The leading row distinguishes this from
  the table's first row. Images remain unclipped outside their cells.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.4.2.3, 20.4.2.10 and 20.4.2.11 define layoutInCell
and positioning bases. Mode 15 treating false like true is the established reference
compatibility divergence. Legacy mixed paragraph Y uses the physical anchor row;
it does not follow the literal first line of the whole table. The independent
multirow controls document this compatibility behavior; source flags are retained.

Supported new subset: numeric page/margin X plus paragraph Y, wrapNone, either
layoutInCell flag. Mixed horizontal alignment and wrapped cell drawings remain
guarded. Existing pure page/margin and column/paragraph behavior is unchanged.
Unit tests compare all native frames, hit testing, paragraph insertion movement,
no-edit parts, text edits, export/reopen and exact undo. Browser tests compare
blue masks bidirectionally within one pixel across all pages before/after edits
and reopening. They do not certify glyph rasterization or all drawing features.
